newsitem.title: USA: Honda unveils electric car to rival GM version.
newsitem.headline: Honda unveils electric car to rival GM version.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd. joined the growing list of electric car makers on Friday by unveiling its EV PLUS -- a four-seat passenger car that will go head-to-head with General Motors Corp.'s EV1 electric car.
Honda officials said the automaker would lease 300 of the vehicles in California over the next three years as a first step toward gauging consumer interest for the environmentally-friendly cars.

However, Honda officials acknowledged the company would lose money on every electric car that it sold until production volumes increased to around 300,000 cars a year, the typical volume for a gasoline-powered vehicle.

"Our goal is to make the EV Plus realistic to lease and at the same time protect the customer from the high development costs of this new technology," Tom Elliott, executive vice president for American Honda, told a news conference at the 1997 Los Angeles Auto Show.
Honda will lease EV PLUS for $499 month over 36 months starting in May 1997. The lease is based on a manufacturer's suggested price of nearly $54,000.

GM's EV1 -- a two-seater with a sticker price near $35,000 -- will lease for less than $500 a month with state and federal subsidies. Without such breaks, EV1 will lease for $640 a month. GM's car is being offered at Saturn dealerships in California and Arizona.
Officials said maintenance costs for both vehicles, including the installation of a recharging unit for the battery, were expected to total about $2,000.
While both cars are aimed at high end buyers, the Honda version uses a more expensive nickel-metal hydride battery, which gives it greater range over Saturn's lead-based battery.
Honda officials said the nickel battery gave their car a "real world" range of 60 to 80 miles per hour, slightly ahead of GM's range at about 50 miles between charges.
Executives of both companies traded barbs during their new conferences Friday, with each side claiming their vehicle was better.
While praising Honda's technology, Saturn officials said the GM entry accelerated faster and was more fun to drive.

"The major difference is this car is very fun to drive," said Joe Kennedy, vice president of Saturn sales and service. "This car has zero to 60 (miles per hour)...in under eight seconds...the Honda vehicle features zero to 60 in the same day."
Honda said it would offer customers a "Charter Lease Program," with unlimited mileage, roadside assistance, and comprehensive insurance.

"We hope to learn what the real values are that consumers associate with the Honda EV PLUS, and what other technology and infrastructure issues are critical to future success," said Robert Bienenfeld, Honda's manager of development in the U.S.
